claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The paper treats a semantic layer as explicit business semantics supplied as context because database schemas do not encode those semantics.
claims.quote: LLMs deployed for natural-language querying of analytical databases suffer from two intertwined failures - incorrect answers and confident hallucinations - both rooted in the same cause: the model is forced to infer business semantics that the schema does not encode. We test whether supplying those semantics as context closes the gap.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The benchmark used 100 natural-language questions over the Cleaned Contoso Retail Dataset in ClickHouse and a paired single-shot protocol.
claims.quote: We benchmark three frontier LLMs (Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4) on 100 natural-language questions over the Cleaned Contoso Retail Dataset in ClickHouse, using a paired single-shot protocol.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Each model was evaluated twice: with schema only, and with schema plus a 4 KB hand-authored markdown document describing measures, conventions, and disambiguation rules.
claims.quote: Each model is evaluated twice: once given only the warehouse schema, and once given the schema plus a 4 KB hand-authored markdown document describing the dataset's measures, conventions, and disambiguation rules.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Adding the semantic-layer document improved accuracy by +17 to +23 percentage points across all three models.
claims.quote: Adding the document improves accuracy by +17 to +23 percentage points across all three models.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: With the document, accuracy was 67.7-68.7%; without it, accuracy was 45.5-50.5%; every cross-cluster comparison was significant at p <0.01.
claims.quote: With it, the three models are statistically indistinguishable (67.7-68.7%); without it, they are also indistinguishable (45.5-50.5%). Every cross-cluster comparison is significant at p <0.01.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The semantic-layer document accounted for essentially all of the significant variance, while model choice within tier did not.
claims.quote: The presence of the semantic-layer document accounts for essentially all of the significant variance; model choice within tier does not.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The authors interpret explicit business semantics as suppressing the dominant class of text-to-SQL errors by changing what the model is asked to do, not by making the model more capable.
claims.quote: We interpret this as a structural result: explicit business semantics suppress the dominant class of text-to-SQL errors not by making the model more capable, but by changing what the model is being asked to do.
